Where do the ECG electrodes go?

PulseLink uses the AD8232 single-lead ECG sensor with 3 pads: RA/R (red, right arm/chest), LA/L (yellow, left arm/chest), and RL/COM (green, right leg/lower abdomen - the reference electrode). For the cleanest signal, place them on the chest: red just below the right collarbone, yellow just below the left collarbone, and green on the lower-left ribcage or lower-right abdomen, away from major muscle. Clean and dry the skin first, and keep still during recording to reduce noise.
How do I pair my ECG device?

Open Device Management from the dashboard and tap \"Add Device\". Turn on your PulseLink AD8232 monitor, keep it within 1-2 metres, and select it once it appears in the scan list. Once paired, the status badge on the dashboard will switch to \"Connected\".
What does an irregular rhythm mean?

An \"irregular rhythm\" flag means the beat-to-beat interval detected during your session fell outside the expected range. This is a screening indicator only, not a diagnosis - share the flagged session with your doctor through the app so they can review the recording.

Sessions recorded offline are queued and sync automatically once you have a stable Wi-Fi or mobile data connection. You can check queued sessions any time from Settings > Offline Sync Status, and tap \"Retry Sync\" if a session has been waiting for a while.
How is my PulseLink ECG monitor powered?

The ESP32-C3 AD8232 ECG monitor is continuously powered via a 5V USB Type-C cable connected to a power adapter or USB port. It does not use internal batteries, ensuring consistent telemetry transmission without degradation over a 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi home network.
My device won\'t connect - what should I check?

Confirm Bluetooth and Wi-Fi are enabled on your phone, that the monitor is powered on (LED lit), and that it isn\'t already connected to another phone. Move within 1-2 metres of the device and try again from Device Management. If it still won\'t connect, restart the monitor by unplugging it for 10 seconds.
How is my health data protected?

Your ECG recordings and profile data are transmitted over an encrypted connection and stored under your account only. Doctors can only view sessions you\'ve been paired with them for. You can review or request removal of your data at any time from Profile > Privacy.

PulseLink\'s ECG monitor uses the AD8232 sensor, a 3-lead (single-channel) front end. Its three pads are commonly labelled RA / LA / RL, or simply R / L / COM on some monitor housings. Follow the steps below for a clean, low-noise recording.
Right arm / right chest, below the collarbone
Left arm / left chest, below the collarbone
Right leg / lower abdomen - reference (ground) electrode
Clean the placement areas with a dry cloth or alcohol wipe. Avoid lotion or oily skin - it weakens the pad\'s adhesive and increases signal noise. Shave the area first if there is heavy hair.
Snap the pads onto the lead cable
Attach each button-snap electrode pad to its lead clip (R/red, L/yellow, COM or RL/green) before sticking it to the skin - pressing the snap on afterward is uncomfortable and can loosen the pad.
Position it on the right side of the chest, just below the collarbone (or on the right forearm for a quick check).
Position it on the left side of the chest, just below the collarbone, mirroring the red pad (or on the left forearm for a quick check).
Position it on the lower-left ribcage or lower-right abdomen, away from the heart\'s axis. This is the reference/ground electrode and doesn\'t need to sit near the other two.
Open a pre-session check from the dashboard. If a pad is loose, the app will flag \"Leads Disconnected\" - press each pad firmly and check the check screen updates to \"Attached\".

Chest placement produces a cleaner, taller QRS signal than the arms/leg placement and is recommended for hospital-style monitoring. Sit still and breathe normally while recording to minimise motion artefacts.
This guide is for using your PulseLink hobbyist ECG monitor and is not a substitute for clinical electrode placement or medical advice.

PulseLink connects patients and clinicians through remote ECG monitoring: capturing heart-rhythm data from a paired device, syncing it securely, and giving doctors timely insight into their patients\' cardiac health.
This application is developed strictly for academic evaluation and clinical prototype assessment; it does not constitute a certified medical diagnostic device.

Responsible party: the PulseLink student development team (Cameron van Heerden and Maxine Palm).

Compliance: PulseLink processes personal information in line with the Protection of Personal Information Act 4 of 2013 (POPIA).

1. Information we process
Account details (name, email, role) and health information, including ECG recordings, heart-rate readings, session notes and device status. Health information is "special personal information" under POPIA and is handled with additional care.

2. Purpose and lawful basis
Data is processed only to provide remote ECG monitoring, clinician review and alerts, and for academic assessment. Processing is based on your consent and is limited to these purposes (purpose specification and minimality).

3. Security safeguards
Data is transmitted over encrypted connections and stored with Firebase services. Access is restricted by authentication and role (patient or doctor), with optional biometric sign-in on your device.

4. Sharing and cross-border transfer
Patient data is visible only to the patient and their treating doctor. It is not sold or used for marketing. Firebase infrastructure may process data outside South Africa; equivalent protection is required in line with POPIA section 72.

5. Retention
Data is retained only while your account is active or as required for assessment, and is deleted on request where the law allows.

6. Your rights
You may request access to, correction of, or deletion of your personal information, withdraw consent, and object to processing. Contact the development team through the GitHub repository.

7. Complaints
You may lodge a complaint with the Information Regulator (South Africa) at inforegulator.org.za.

1. Acceptance
By using PulseLink you agree to these terms.

2. Academic prototype
PulseLink is a student project built for academic evaluation and clinical prototype assessment. It is not a certified medical device and must not be used to diagnose, treat or monitor any medical condition.

3. Emergencies
In a medical emergency, contact your local emergency services immediately (South Africa: 112 or 10177). Do not rely on this app for emergency response.

4. Your responsibilities
Provide accurate information, keep your credentials confidential, and use the app only for lawful purposes. Doctors remain fully responsible for their own clinical judgement.

5. No warranty
The app is provided "as is" without warranties of any kind. Readings, alerts and reports may be delayed, incomplete or inaccurate.

6. Limitation of liability
To the extent permitted by South African law, the authors and their institution are not liable for any loss or harm arising from use of the app.

7. Intellectual property
The PulseLink name, emblem and source code are the work of the authors and are shared through the project GitHub repository under its stated licence.

8. Changes and governing law
These terms may be updated as the project evolves. They are governed by the laws of the Republic of South Africa.
